selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What time of day is this passage about?
questions.answer: Sunset, the time of Maghrib.

questions.question: What happens to the beautiful living things from summer and fall when this time comes?
questions.answer: They pass away and disappear as winter begins.

questions.question: What sad human event does sunset make a person remember?
questions.answer: A person’s death and leaving loved ones behind.

questions.question: Where does the passage say a person goes after death?
questions.answer: To the grave.

questions.question: What big event for the world does this time also bring to mind?
questions.answer: The world will come to an end, and its people will move on to other worlds.

questions.question: What image shows that this world’s test time will end?
questions.answer: Its lamp will be put out.

questions.question: What kind of things are warned against in this passage?
questions.answer: Loving temporary things too much and treating them like they should be worshipped.

questions.question: Why is the warning strong at sunset?
questions.answer: Because sunset shows that beautiful things in this world do not last.

questions.question: What is one main idea of the passage?
questions.answer: This time reminds people that life in this world is short and they should not cling to things that fade away.

questions.question: If someone only loves things that do not last, what lesson should he learn from this passage?
questions.answer: He should remember that those things will go away and turn his heart toward what lasts.

questions.question: Which prayer time is described in the target passage?
questions.answer: Maghrib, at sunset.

questions.question: What season starts when the lovely things mentioned in the passage disappear?
questions.answer: Winter.

questions.question: How are those good-byes described?
questions.answer: They are sad and full of parting.

questions.question: What does sunset help us think about in a person’s life?
questions.answer: That one day each person will die.

questions.question: How are the people a dying person loves affected?
questions.answer: They are left in sadness.

questions.question: What happens to the people of the world when the world ends, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They move to other worlds.

questions.question: What does the passage say will happen to the light of this world’s testing place?
questions.answer: It will be turned off.

questions.question: Who especially needs the warning in this passage?
questions.answer: People who give their hearts to things that are only here for a short time.

questions.question: What does the word “transient” mean here?
questions.answer: Not lasting; going away after a short time.

questions.question: What feeling does the passage give about sunset: only joy, only silliness, or a serious reminder?
questions.answer: A serious reminder.

questions.question: What natural change at day’s end begins this passage?
questions.answer: The sun is setting.

questions.question: What does this time remind people about summer and fall?
questions.answer: Their beauty fades and comes to an end.

questions.question: What lesson about this world can children learn from that picture?
questions.answer: Pretty things in this world do not stay forever.

questions.question: What personal change does the passage connect with this time of day?
questions.answer: A person leaving this life through death.
